narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 88.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt if admitted. That is a prediction, not a judgment of your worth, but it was high enough to drive the denial.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you are in the lowest decile (1.00), while accepted students averaged around 5.79. That very low rank pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. The second most influential factor was your admission test score of 25, well below the accepted-student average of about 37.18, which also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.50 was above the accepted average of 3.23, so it helped move the prediction toward passing, but it was not enough to outweigh the other two factors.

To proceed, ask admissions for a review of your file and discuss any circumstances behind your class rank and test score. Consider retaking the admission test after structured preparation, and provide evidence of improved academic or bar-readiness skills, such as a study plan, additional coursework, or work experience. If possible, reapply after strengthening those areas, and request feedback so your next application directly addresses the concerns that drove this decision.
